question: A financial institution can be a banking institution only when it __________.

options.text: performs both the functions of ‘accepting deposits’ and ‘advancing loans’
performs the function of ‘accepting deposits’ and not ‘advancing loans’
neither performs the function of ’accepting deposits’ nor of ‘advancing loans’
performs the function of ‘advancing loans’ and not ‘accepting deposits’

solution:
The correct answer is to __**perform**____** both the functions of ‘accepting deposits’ and ‘advancing loans’.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Banking institutions, also known as** banks**, are financial institutions that **accept deposits from customers and use those deposits to make loans to other customers.**
 
• They also offer a variety of other financial services, such as checking and savings accounts, money transfers, and investment products.
 
• There are two main types of banking institutions:
 
 
• **Commercial banks:** Commercial banks are the most common type of bank. They **offer a wide range of financial services** to individuals and businesses.
 
• **Investment banks:** Investment banks focus on providing financial services to **corporations and institutional investors.** They help companies raise capital through **underwriting and selling securities**, and they provide advice on mergers and acquisitions.
 
 
 
• Banking institutions **earn money by charging interest on the loans they make.**
 
• They also earn money from** fees, such as ATM fees, overdraft fees, and account maintenance fees.**
